name: Harlow_Creek_OM_Agreement_2018.pdf
pages:
OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT
City of Harlow Creek, Georgia and Northline Contract Operations, Inc.

2.1 Term. Ten years from 1 July 2018 to 30 June 2028.

3.1 Scope of services. The Operator shall operate and maintain (a) the Harlow Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant, (b) the wastewater collection system including 14 lift stations, and (c) biosolids handling, hauling and disposal.

9.4 Capital improvements. Capital repairs and replacements above $25,000 per item, including odor control equipment and media, are the responsibility of the City. The Operator shall recommend such improvements in the annual capital plan.

9.6 Odor. The Operator shall operate the odor control systems as installed and respond to each odor complaint within one business day.

14.1 Limitation of liability. The Operator's total liability under this Agreement in any contract year shall not exceed the annual fee for that year.

14.2 [Reserved.]

15.1 Indemnification. The Operator shall indemnify the City against third party claims to the extent caused by the negligence or wilful misconduct of the Operator.

Analyst note: 14.1 is a liability cap and 15.1 limits indemnity to negligence. There is no waiver of consequential, special or punitive damages anywhere in the Agreement or its three amendments. One of the three core terms is missing: rating 3, for Legal to confirm.

16.3 Claims. Where a third party claim names both parties, the parties shall cooperate in the defense and may agree a joint defense.

21.1 Termination for convenience. The City may terminate this Agreement on 180 days' written notice.
evidence_for: Non-negotiable terms read (liability cap, consequential damages, indemnity), the scope of services, who funds odor control, and how the City can end it.

name: Baines_Ortega_Demand_Letter_2026-11-19.pdf
author: L. Ortega
pages:
BAINES & ORTEGA LLP
19 November 2026

By email and certified mail
Northline Contract Operations, Inc., Legal Department
cc: City Attorney, City of Harlow Creek

Re: Notice of claim and demand, Harlow Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant

We represent 23 residents of the Mill Pond and Eastgate neighbourhoods. Since May 2026 our clients have suffered recurring noxious odors from the plant and from biosolids hauling, which interfere with the use and enjoyment of their homes. Six complaints were made to the plant this year; two received no reply.

Our clients demand that within 30 days Northline (1) abate the odors, (2) provide the odor logs and complaint records since January 2024, and (3) enter into discussions on compensation. Failing this we are instructed to file an action for nuisance and negligence in the Superior Court of the county, naming Northline and the City.

Please preserve all records relating to odor control, operator rounds, biosolids load-out and complaints.
evidence_for: A written demand before suit: under the scorecard's bands this rates Threatened litigation at 4.

name: Calder_Valley_Loss_Review_2026-03.pdf
author: Tom Brandvold
pages:
CALDER VALLEY WWTP: REVIEW OF THE LOST RENEWAL
Prepared for the Contract Operations leadership team, March 2026

We operated Calder Valley for eleven years without a notice of violation. The County re-bid the contract in 2025 and awarded it to Clearbrook Operations in December. Our price was 4% above theirs.

What changed in the year before:
  March 2025    The utilities director who signed both renewals retired.
  May 2025      The County hired a procurement adviser to "test the market".
  March 2025    The NPS survey went to the retired director's address; no answer was recorded and the last score (9) stayed on file.
  September 2025 Clearbrook presented to the County Commission.
What we would do differently: meet a new client lead within 30 days; treat a score given by a predecessor as no score; read the commission agendas. Plant performance was never the issue.
evidence_for: What the record showed in the year before a renewal was lost, to test the scorecard against it.

name: Claims_Notice_and_Legal_Hold_Procedure.pdf
author: Elliot Marsh
pages:
CLAIMS NOTICE AND LEGAL HOLD

1. A written demand or pre-suit notice goes to Legal within one working day.
2. Legal issues a document hold the same day.
3. The insurer is notified within 30 days of a written demand.
4. After a demand, contact with the claimants about the matter goes through Legal. Routine service contact (returning a complaint call) continues, logged.
5. The client is told where the contract requires it or the client is also named.
evidence_for: What must happen when a written demand arrives, and what may be said to residents.

name: Residents near treatment plant say the smell is back
author: Staff reporter
pages:
harlowcreekledger.example/news/treatment-plant-odor

HARLOW CREEK LEDGER, 12 November 2026

Residents near treatment plant say the smell is back

Neighbours on Mill Pond Road say odors from the city wastewater plant have returned on weekday afternoons. "We called twice this month and nobody called back," said one resident. Council candidate Dee Lanier said the city "should look hard at who runs that plant". The city said odor control equipment is scheduled for replacement "when funding allows". The plant is operated for the city by Northline.

Analyst reading: negative. Fourth negative article of nine in twelve months.
evidence_for: Local coverage of the plant: counted in the media share, and read for what residents and candidates say.

author: Staff reporter

ASHBY FALLS COURIER, 19 November 2026

Town weighs running its own water plants as contract nears end

With the operations contract ending in June, DPW Director Karen Whitlock told the Finance Committee the town should "look at every option, including doing it ourselves". Clearbrook Operations, which took over neighbouring Dunmere Ridge in April, presented to the committee in October. Northline, the current operator, was not at the meeting.

Analyst reading: negative. Two of six articles in twelve months are negative.
evidence_for: Local coverage and who is quoted: one more negative article, and a competitor in the room.
